headline: US stocks closed lower as stronger GDP and PCE data followed Fed rate hold while heavy AI spending and earnings resets weighed on tech
raw_text:
- The S&P 500 ($SPX) fell about 0.3% to 7,720, the Dow ($DJI) slipped about 0.25% to 52,343, the Nasdaq 100 ($NDX) lost roughly 1.4%, while the Russell 2000 (IWM) climbed about 1% and finished higher.
- Alphabet (GOOGL) dropped about 13% after Q3 revenue of $127.6 billion missed estimates on slower search and advertising growth and the company reported roughly $9.1 billion in negative free cash flow tied to heavy AI capex.
- Alphabet maintained a full-year capex outlook of $195–205 billion and disclosed AI-related commitments exceeding $900 billion, reviving investor concerns over the scale of AI spending.
- ServiceNow (NOW) fell around 27% after a Q3 profit miss and underwhelming Q4 guidance, while Fortinet (FTNT) declined about 20% after cutting its full-year service revenue forecast.
- Marvell Technology (MRVL) declined about 13% on reports of advanced talks to acquire Lumentum (LITE), adding to pressure in semiconductor names.
- Caterpillar (CAT) lost about 9% despite beating EPS estimates with $7.20 and posting record Q3 sales, as investor concerns about the sustainability of AI data-center spending weighed on AI-exposed industrials.
- Eli Lilly (LLY) gained around 7% after posting Q3 revenue of $24.4 billion versus $22.62 billion expected and raising its full-year sales forecast for the third time on strong Zepbound demand.
- Crocs (CROX) jumped 25% after raising its 2026 outlook and citing a turnaround in its HEYDUDE brand, while Glaukos (GKOS) rallied 33% on record Q3 sales of $211 million versus $168 million expected.
- The Bureau of Economic Analysis reported Q3 GDP growth of 3.4% and a September PCE price index gain of 0.5% month-over-month and 3.6% year-over-year, following the Fed’s decision a day earlier to hold rates at 3.75–4%.
- DoorDash (DASH) announced a $17 billion acquisition of Instacart after beating Q3 estimates, while Amazon (AMZN) and Intel (INTC) reported earnings after the close and both declined sharply in extended trading.
